text:
Priya M: heads up — provisioning spike in eu-west1, ~12 nodes stuck in a "suspend" state, GPUs not attaching to kubelet. trying to triage, looks correlated with last-night BMC fw roll (v2.1.4 -> v2.2.0)
Alex G: ack. any error on the node side? pod logs or kubelet?
Priya M: kubelet shows `container runtime not ready`, dmesg shows NVMe init OK but we see repeated BMC watchdog resets in the host logs. sample from one node:```Jan 21 03:12:01 host bmc[123]: watchdog: reset requested
Jan 21 03:12:02 host kernel: bmc-irq: MC reset
Jan 21 03:12:03 host systemd[1]: Started Bring up BMC.
Jan 21 03:12:04 host bios: SecureBoot: flag toggled -> ON
Jan 21 03:12:05 host bios: microcode: reverify SPD @0x50 failed
Jan 21 03:12:06 host systemd[1]: Node entered suspend state
```
oncall-jen: infra-bot reported mass reprovisioning alerts at 03:15 UTC.
Taylor R: weird that BIOS secureboot flips mid-boot. looks like SPD read fail -> BIOS pulls fallback microcode -> secureboot state recomputed -> OS refuses to start drivers?
Dan S: could be a race between the new BMC fw and the motherboard SPD timing. we saw similar on a lab board when BMC toggled pwrseq too early.
Alex G: are canaries affected?
Priya M: canaries (eu1-small) are fine — only racks with certain ASRock X9 variants hit. 12 nodes across 3 racks.
Taylor R: immediate plan: pause the v2.2.0 BMC rollout, mark the affected rack firmware pinned to v2.1.4 and reprovision them with `--force-bmc-fw=2.1.4`. also, hold autoscaler from adding new jobs to those racks.
Dan S: +1. I'll open a rollback patch on the firmware job and kick a rollback playbook.
Priya M: commands I'm running: `ipmitool -I lanplus -H $BMC -U admin -P **** mc info` and `journalctl -u bmc-fw-updater -n 200`. found these repeated logs: `ERR: SPD read timeout` and `WARN: watchdog heartbeat missed`
Alex G: if SPD read timeout is the root cause, is there a mitigation in BIOS settings? maybe extend SPD timing or disable SPD a priori? but that would be vendor-specific.
oncall-jen: infra-bot: 03:20 UTC - Created incident INC-2026-128, severity: sev2, assigned: Dan S
Taylor R: action items: 1) pause rollout (Dan) 2) pin affected racks to 2.1.4 (Priya) 3) run `ipmi sol` capture while reprovisioning to catch early boot (Alex) 4) escalate to vendor (Taylor)
Dan S: starting pause now. annulling staged jobs for v2.2.0 in eu-west1: `./fwctl pause --region eu-west1 --tag bmc-2.2.0`
Priya M: pinning racks: `fleetctl set-meta rack=eu-west1-r3 bmc-fw=2.1.4` and kicking reprovision `provision --rack eu-west1-r3 --force` (doing one node at a time).
Alex G: I'll attach `ipmitool sel list` output to the incident. looking for repeating SEL entries around 03:12.
Taylor R: cost note: autoscaler queued ~320 jobs waiting for GPUs, we had to spin up a temporary cloud burst cluster (cost estimate $480/hr) to keep latency below SLO. need to capture that in the postmortem.
Priya M: confirmed: reprovision of node-472 completed after pin -> node came to ready and GPUs attached. backtrace shows that the BMC stopped toggling the power sequence during BIOS init.
Dan S: reopening vendor support ticket with full SOL capture + SEL + BMC fw binary diff (v2.1.4 vs v2.2.0). tagging: @asrock-support @vendor-firmware
Alex G: quick diagnostic checklist for oncall: 1) check `ipmitool mc info` 2) `ipmitool sel list` 3) `journalctl -u bmc-fw-updater` 4) verify `secureboot` status in BIOS console 5) pin fw if unstable
oncall-jen: infra-bot: 03:34 UTC - Noted that 8/12 nodes recovered after pin, 4 still reprovisioning.
Priya M: trying a slower reprovision cadence on remaining 4. doing `sleep 45` between IPMI power-cycles. so far one came up but in degraded state (two GPUs offline).
Taylor R: for the degraded GPU state, capture `nvidia-smi -q` + `dmesg | grep -i nvidia` before reboots. could be driver init ordering with the BIOS microcode path.
Dan S: long-term: add hw-compatibility filter to the firmware rollout (exclude ASRock X9 revision <= B). also add SPD read watchdog fuzzing to the CI lab.
Priya M: noting postmortem owners: Taylor (root cause), Alex (detection & tooling), Dan (rollout safeguards), Priya (remediation & cost).
Alex G: any ETA on vendor reply?
Taylor R: vendor acknowledged, will triage tomorrow EOD. asked for SEL + SOL + full BMC logs (pushed via secure vendor-share).
oncall-jen: infra-bot: 03:55 UTC - Incident INC-2026-128 moved to "investigation".
Dan S: leaving a temporary note in runbook: `If BMC fw causes SPD-timeout->secureboot flip, pin to previous fw, slow power cycles, and contact vendor.`
Priya M: thanks team. I'm keeping the last node under reprovision watch. will update the incident. :thumbsup:
Alex G: thanks — please ping if it starts popping elsewhere.
Taylor R: added cost impact estimate to the incident ticket.
Priya M: closing thread here, continuing in INC-2026-128.
